data.narrative:
Lumaril is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Mark Elliot and Ben Duffield that has raised $12M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a competitive set of 9 private companies and 1 public peer (277810.KQ) in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including comparables such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

A stage-progression methodology was applied, using the $12M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement. This approach yielded an implied valuation of $30M. A peer-median analysis was not viable due to insufficient clustering within narrow filters: while 10 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three qualified under same-stage or adjacent-stage and similar-valuation-tier criteria, making a narrow peer comparison unreliable.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, with a median of $30M. This range reflects reliance on a single methodological anchor and carries material uncertainty tied to the absence of tightly comparable seed-stage peers in the robotics sector. Key variables affecting valuation within this band include technology differentiation, go-to-market progress since the $12M raise, and fundraising velocity toward Series A.
